subject.title: Gateway auto-injects toolsAllow into isolated agentTurn crons; null patch doesn't clear it; breaks CLI backend

question: Should a restricted creator-surface cron update be allowed to clear an auto-stamped `toolsAllow`, or must that cap remain mandatory to preserve the cron tool-policy boundary from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91499?
rationale: The source can be changed mechanically, but the correct behavior depends on maintainer intent for a security-sensitive boundary between explicit user clear semantics, restricted creator policy, and CLI backends that cannot enforce runtime `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Keep mandatory cap with explicit feedback
options.body: Preserve the restricted creator-surface cap and make `toolsAllow: null` either re-stamp as a default-marked cap or return a clear validation message instead of silently looking like a raw clear.

options.title: Allow clears only for trusted scopes
options.body: Permit raw operator or unrestricted Gateway callers to clear `toolsAllow`, while keeping restricted creator-surface cron tool calls capped.

options.title: Remove the default cap for CLI crons
options.body: Stop stamping defaults for isolated CLI-backed cron jobs, accepting the security-boundary change only if owners explicitly approve it.

recommendation.title: Keep mandatory cap with explicit feedback
recommendation.body: Preserve the restricted creator-surface cap and make `toolsAllow: null` either re-stamp as a default-marked cap or return a clear validation message instead of silently looking like a raw clear.

likelyOwner.reason: This user is tied to the recent default-marker and cron-service follow-up commits on the affected boundary.
